solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: the word is to be said aloud, and said the way a drunk slurs it

blocks.note: breaks are snaps; slur 'snaps' as a drunk would and it comes out as 'shnaps'

annotation.surface: A question about the pauses a tipsy person takes between rounds.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that a drunk turns every S into SH, so SNAPS becomes the spirit they are drinking.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is one particular German-style spirit, and the clue names only the broad class it belongs to.

indicators.note: the second drink is placed after the first

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark beer

annotation.surface: A campaigner calling for one drink after another.
annotation.walkthrough: Both drinks come from the same word, once as a verb (SUP) and once as a beer (PORTER).
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as nouns: someone who argues publicly for a cause or person backs it.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
with puts the two pieces side by side

blocks.note: EH is 'what?', said when you did not hear
ave is the Latin greeting 'hail'

annotation.surface: A puzzled question about what is going on with a greeting that has been thrown.
annotation.walkthrough: 'What’s up' reads as one question, but it splits: 'What' is EH, and 'up' turns it over in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as a verb: both mean to throw with effort, as with a line or a stone.

clue.text: A hint to enter junction? The opposite (8)

indicators.note: the hint goes inside the junction

blocks.note: taken as it stands
a node is a point where lines meet
a tip is a hint

annotation.surface: Directions telling a driver to take a hint and join the road, then saying to do the reverse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' seems to reverse the instruction before it; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Literally the point on the far side of the globe, the word is extended to mean the exact contrary of anything.

blocks.note: not the bird but a verb: in American use, a past form of 'dive', as in 'have dove'
also a verb, not a bird: 'swallow' as printed is the present tense, not a past form

annotation.surface: Birdwatching: this bird might be a dove, but it is not a swallow.
annotation.walkthrough: Dove and swallow look like two birds, but both are verbs here. In American use 'dove' is heard as a past form of dive, as in 'have dove', while 'swallow' is not a past form at all.
annotation.definitionFit: A past participle is the verb form used after 'have', which dove can be and swallow cannot.

indicators.note: AS is placed around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as it stands
an abyss is a void, an empty gulf

annotation.surface: Hedgerows growing round the edge of a chasm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hedges' looks like the plant noun; it is the verb, as in dodging a question.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who hedges avoids giving a straight answer.

clue.text: In truth, so full of it (6)

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

blocks.note: so and very both mean extremely
taken as it stands

annotation.surface: An accusation that someone who claims to tell the truth is really full of nonsense.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In truth' reads as 'truly', but 'In' is only the link and 'truth' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in a literary register, from the Latin for true.

clue.text: Paramour soon gets a sailor put up (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

blocks.note: 'in a mo' is informal British for soon
A plus TAR, the stock sailor

annotation.surface: A lover is about to have a sailor to stay for the night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put up' suggests giving the sailor a bed; in a down entry it turns the letters over.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the Italian-derived word names a woman who is someone's lover, usually an illicit one.

blocks.note: the past tense of slay
an American word for a large number of things

annotation.surface: A grim report of a massacre of Americans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'of Americans' marks the second sense as American usage: 'a lot', as Americans say it.
annotation.definitionFit: Slew is the past of slay, and in the US a slew of things is a lot of them.

indicators.note: the fodder is set running, jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A runner is still in contention and going strong.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 10 across, PLANT.
annotation.definitionFit: The carline thistle is a wild plant of dry grassland.

blocks.note: a works is a factory, a noun
an agent placed secretly inside an organisation

annotation.surface: Someone takes a job undercover.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Works' reads as a verb; it is the noun for a factory.
annotation.definitionFit: Plant means both an industrial works and a planted spy.

clue.text: Car seat is adapted for internal flight (9)

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new form

blocks.note: the nine letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A car seat is being modified for use on a domestic plane journey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'internal flight' suggests a domestic air trip; it is a flight of stairs inside a house.
annotation.definitionFit: A staircase is a flight of stairs inside a building.

clue.text: Prevail upon to spread after zero crowding (14)

indicators.note: the letters are spread out and rearranged
the jumbled letters come after the zero

blocks.note: zero looks like the letter O
the thirteen letters rearranged

annotation.surface: Persuading someone to fan out after nobody is left crowding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prevail upon' reads as persuade; it is only letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Overpopulation is too many people in one place, a crowding.

indicators.note: the second piece parts the first, splitting it open

blocks.note: a thing is a tool or gadget
under a figure means short of it

annotation.surface: A fine musical instrument missing some of its components.
annotation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun for components; it is the verb, splitting THING. 'Thundering' is informal British for very great, as in 'a thundering nuisance'.
annotation.definitionFit: Thundering is an informal intensifier meaning great or tremendous.

clue.text: Virgin turned off when drinking tea (9)

indicators.note: off means wrong, so the letters are rearranged
the jumbled letters take the tea inside

blocks.note: the six letters rearranged
cha is a British word for tea

annotation.surface: Someone who has never tried it is put off by the sight of people drinking tea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' suggests a person; here it means untouched, as in virgin territory.
annotation.definitionFit: Virgin land is uncharted, not yet explored or mapped.

blocks.note: a periodic gathering of traders and stalls
an adjective here: honest, just, as in a square deal

annotation.surface: A market square in a town centre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Market square' reads as one place; it splits into two separate meanings of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a noun for a periodic gathering of traders, and an adjective meaning honest, as in a square deal.

clue.text: Leaf pest taking a rest under rose (3,6)

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means placed below, so it comes second

blocks.note: rose as a colour, a shade of red
in snooker a spider is a cue rest with raised legs

annotation.surface: A garden bug settling down to rest beneath a rose bush.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts the pest on a rose bush, but 'rose' is the colour. A snooker player uses a spider rest to reach over balls, and red is a snooker ball too.
annotation.definitionFit: The red spider mite is a tiny pest that feeds on leaves.

clue.text: Out of work, play with new guide (8)

indicators.note: the play sits outside the work, holding it
the new letter is added alongside

blocks.note: a drama is a play
to go is to work, as when a machine will not go
N is the standard abbreviation for new

annotation.surface: An unemployed actor filling time with a new play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of work' reads as one phrase meaning unemployed, but it splits: 'Out of' is a position instruction, and 'work' is the verb, as in a plan that works.
annotation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an interpreter and guide in Arabic, Turkish or Persian-speaking lands.

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

blocks.note: a frock is a dress; drop the F

annotation.surface: Causing a stir by turning up in a dress with no top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'topless' paints a risqué outfit; it only takes the first letter off the dress.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: news that shakes someone to the core leaves them stunned.

clue.text: The sticks, I suggest, to deliver (10)

blocks.note: whoever says 'I suggest' is a hinter, one who hints
to land a blow or a deal is to deliver it

annotation.surface: A hesitant suggestion that the firewood should be delivered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I suggest' describes the speaker, a hinter. 'The sticks' is slang for remote country, not firewood.
annotation.definitionFit: The hinterland is the remote back country, the sticks.

clue.text: Because about to open mouth, feasts (6)

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second

blocks.note: as can mean because
to gape is to open the mouth wide

annotation.surface: People about to start eating, mouths open, because of the banquets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but the two words belong to different pieces: 'about' is the wrapping instruction and 'to' starts the verb phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Agapes were the communal love feasts of the early Christians.

indicators.note: the shard comes after the winning

blocks.note: save and bar both mean except
gaining is winning
a chip is a small broken piece

annotation.surface: A plea to preserve the Shard once a planning battle has been won.
annotation.walkthrough: The Shard is a London skyscraper, so the capital makes it look like a proper noun; it is just a broken fragment.
annotation.definitionFit: A bargaining chip is something one can concede in a negotiation.

clue.text: Native Americans heading for Texas get lost (3,2)

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the Hopi are a people of Arizona
first letter of Texas

annotation.surface: A group of Native Americans loses its way on the road to Texas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hop it' is British slang for 'go away'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both 'get lost' and 'hop it' are rude ways of telling someone to leave.

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
to outfit is to equip, to arm

annotation.surface: A loving wife receives a new set of clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'outfit' reads as clothes; it is the verb, to equip.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: heat stands for kindness and fondness, as in a hearty welcome.

clue.text: George in paradise, almost cutting a great deal (9)

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped
the shortened word cuts into the other piece

blocks.note: a lot is a great deal
utopia is a paradise, without its last A

annotation.surface: A man named George, in heaven, nearly ruining a big business deal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'George' is pilots' slang for the automatic pilot, so the name looks like a person but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: George is an old nickname for an aircraft's autopilot.

indicators.note: the teenager straddles the exercise, one leg each side

blocks.note: Mods were a British youth cult of the 1960s
PE is physical education

annotation.surface: A young person sitting on an exercise bike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'exercise bike' reads as one gym machine; the words belong to different parts.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a light motorised cycle with pedals is one kind of bike.

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
a dish is prepared food

annotation.surface: A doctor brings in food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a stray preposition; it is the definition, meaning fashionable.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal adjective: what is in is fashionable, as in 'the in crowd'.

clue.text: Eye cast over this month’s Irish players (8)

indicators.note: the glance is laid over the other piece, covering it on both sides

blocks.note: a leer is a sly look cast at someone
inst. is short for instant, business language for this month

annotation.surface: Someone takes a look at this month's Irish team sheet.
annotation.walkthrough: Leinster is an Irish province and its rugby union team.
annotation.definitionFit: Leinster Rugby is one of Ireland's professional rugby sides.
